response: Juvenile ankylosing spondylitis (JAS) is not exactly the same disease as adult ankylosing spondylitis (AAS). While they share some similarities, there are distinct differences in their onset and progression. JAS tends to have an onset more often with oligoarthritis and enthesitis, whereas AAS typically begins with spinal disease. Additionally, hip and knee joint involvement is more common in JAS than in AAS. These differences suggest that JAS and AAS may have different underlying mechanisms or pathways, although they are related conditions within the broader category of spondyloarthritis.
